name: Hip flexor stretching (couch stretch)
lead: Hip flexor stretching is a flexibility practice aimed at the muscles at the front of the hip, chiefly the iliopsoas and the rectus femoris of the quadriceps. The couch stretch is a popular variation in which the rear knee is placed on the floor with the shin braced up against a couch, wall or bench, so that the hip is held in extension while the front of the thigh is lengthened. [1]

In looksmaxxing and posture circles the stretch is discussed mainly as a way to reduce anterior pelvic tilt, a posture in which the front of the pelvis drops relative to the back. Proponents attribute this pattern partly to shortened hip flexors from prolonged sitting. [2][3]

Published research on hip flexor stretching has mostly looked at flexibility and athletic performance rather than pelvic posture or facial and body appearance. A 2021 systematic review with meta-analysis examined stretching of the hip flexors and performance parameters, and a small laboratory study examined hip extension range of motion and vertical jump. [4][5] No trial found in this search tests the couch stretch specifically as a treatment for anterior pelvic tilt.

paras: The iliopsoas, formed by the psoas major and iliacus, is described as the strongest hip flexor and as a postural muscle with a high share of slow-twitch fibers. It runs from the lumbar spine and pelvis to the femur. [6] In the couch stretch the rear hip is brought toward extension while the knee is bent, which also loads the rectus femoris, a quadriceps muscle that crosses both the hip and knee.

Practitioners usually hold the position for a period of time per side and sometimes add a trunk tilt or glute contraction. General guidance on pace and duration varies between coaches and is not standardised.

Anatomically, the iliopsoas is a composite of the psoas major, which arises from the lumbar vertebrae and discs, and the iliacus, which arises from the iliac fossa; the two usually merge in the thigh and attach to the femur's lesser trochanter. It is supplied by lumbar spinal nerves L1 to L3 and the femoral nerve, and Wikipedia calls it the prime mover of hip flexion, important for standing, walking and running [6]. Because it links the lumbar spine and femur, problems in either region can affect it [6].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and posture culture
paras: Anterior pelvic tilt is often described in online posture communities as making the stomach protrude and the lower back arch, and some say it affects perceived height. Hip flexor stretching is one of the standard counter-measures listed alongside glute strengthening and core work. [2] Encyclopedic sources describe this stretch-and-strengthen pairing as the usual corrective approach to lumbar hyperlordosis, while noting that the supporting references are limited. [2][3]

Wikipedia's pelvic tilt article defines anterior tilt as the front of the pelvis dropping relative to the back, associated with shortened hip flexors and lengthened hip extensors and also called lumbar hyperlordosis [2]. It lists the usual approach as strengthening the glutes, core and lower back while stretching the hip flexors, with glute bridges, planks, dead bugs and hip thrusts as examples; the article itself is flagged for needing more citations [2]. Posterior tilt is described as the opposite pattern, with lengthened hip flexors and shortened hip extensors, which is why guidance in this area differs by pelvic position and a stretch is not applied to everyone [2]. Lateral tilt is linked to scoliosis or unequal leg length and is managed by addressing the cause [2].

The Wikipedia entry on the iliopsoas notes that a short, tight iliopsoas is thought to contribute to pain in the low back, sacroiliac joint, hip and groin, but it does not cover stretching techniques. [6]

The authors of the 2021 meta-analysis open from the premise that tight hip flexors can contribute to lumbar spine pain and that sedentary behaviour limits hip extension flexibility; the review looked at performance outcomes rather than posture. [4]

The 2021 meta-analysis reviewed studies of hip flexor stretching on performance parameters, and the small laboratory study found that changes in passive hip flexor compliance did not explain a vertical-jump improvement after static stretching [4][5]. A 2026 randomised trial of high-volume stretching examined stretch-mediated muscle growth, strength and balance, a different line of work that treats stretching as a training stimulus [7]. Wikipedia notes that a short, tight iliopsoas can present with externally rotated legs and pain in the low or mid back, sacroiliac joint, hip, groin, thigh or knee [6].

No studies found on the couch stretch itself as a posture or appearance intervention. Related research on hip flexor stretching in general includes a 2021 systematic review with meta-analysis of stretching effects on performance parameters [4]; a laboratory study of 15 participants that compared pre-exercise static hip flexor stretching with hip extension range of motion and vertical jump height, whose title reports that changes in passive hip flexor compliance did not account for the jump improvement [5]; and a 2026 randomized controlled trial of high-volume, high-intensity stretching and its effects on muscle growth, strength and dynamic balance [7]. None of these measured pelvic tilt or appearance.

No adverse-event data specific to the couch stretch were found. Because the position loads the knee and the front of the hip, coaches often describe an intensity ramp-up, and people with knee or hip conditions are commonly told to consult a clinician; this is general exercise guidance rather than findings from a trial.

card.summary: A kneeling quad-and-hip-flexor stretch used to counter anterior pelvic tilt; popular in posture circles, with no trials on that use.
card.note: Research covers flexibility and performance, not pelvic tilt or appearance.

quick.overview:
The couch stretch holds the rear hip in extension with the knee bent to lengthen the hip flexors and front thigh. It is widely recommended in posture and looksmaxxing communities as a fix for anterior pelvic tilt.

Trials of hip flexor stretching have looked at flexibility and athletic performance. No study found tests it for pelvic tilt or appearance.
quick.mechanism: The stretch is thought to lengthen the iliopsoas and rectus femoris, which proponents say pull the pelvis forward when shortened by long periods of sitting.
quick.risks: No specific harms are documented. The position loads the knee and hip, and general guidance advises people with joint problems to seek clinical advice.

chain: Rear hip is held in extension with the front thigh lengthened
Hip flexor length and hip extension range are worked on
Pelvis sits less tipped forward alongside glute and core work
Flatter stomach line and more upright posture
angle.text: People use the couch stretch to lengthen the iliopsoas and quadriceps and to counter the forward pelvic tilt they associate with long sitting. Combined with glute and core strengthening, it is aimed at a more upright stance and a less protruding stomach and arched lower back.
